claim: Ribosome stalling on mRNAs can decrease protein expression.
source: Ribosome stalling on mRNAs can decrease protein expression.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by the experimental work presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ribosomes move at an average speed of 3–20 codons per second during translation elongation in vivo.
source: Ribosomes move at an average speed of 3–20 codons per second during translation elongation in vivo (Dalbow and Young, 1975; Bonven and Gulløv, 1979; Yan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The typical initiation rate of ribosomes on mRNAs is less than 1 s-1.
source: Since this rate is higher than the typical initiation rate of ribosomes on mRNAs [less than 1 s-1 (Yan et al., 2016; Kennell and Riezman, 1977)], elongation is often assumed to not affect the expression level of most proteins.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Elongation is often assumed to not affect the expression level of most proteins.
source: Since this rate is higher than the typical initiation rate of ribosomes on mRNAs [less than 1 s-1 (Yan et al., 2016; Kennell and Riezman, 1977)], elongation is often assumed to not affect the expression level of most proteins.
evidence: This is a statement about common assumptions in the field, supported by the logical inference from the rate comparison.

claim: The elongation rate of ribosomes can decrease significantly at specific locations on an mRNA due to low abundance of aminoacyl-tRNAs, inhibitory codon pairs or amino acid pairs, nascent peptides interacting strongly with the ribosome exit tunnel, or the presence of RNA-binding proteins.
source: Nevertheless, the elongation rate of ribosomes can decrease significantly at specific locations on an mRNA due to low abundance of aminoacyl-tRNAs, inhibitory codon pairs or amino acid pairs, nascent peptides interacting strongly with the ribosome exit tunnel, or the presence of RNA-binding proteins (Richter and Coller, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous review.

claim: Ribosome profiling has enabled the identification of additional factors that induce slowing or stalling of ribosomes during elongation.
source: Ribosome profiling — the deep sequencing of ribosome-protected mRNA fragments — has enabled the identification of additional factors that induce slowing or stalling of ribosomes during elongation (Ingolia et al., 2009; Ingolia, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on ribosome profiling.

claim: In the traffic jam model, the duration of ribosome stalling is sufficiently long to induce a queue of trailing ribosomes extending to the start codon, thus decreasing the translation initiation rate.
source: In the widely used traffic jam model (MacDonald et al., 1968), the duration of ribosome stalling is sufficiently long to induce a queue of trailing ribosomes extending to the start codon, thus decreasing the translation initiation rate.
evidence: This claim describes a mechanistic model and is supported by a citation to the original model.

claim: Evidence supporting the traffic jam model has been found in the context of EF-P dependent polyproline stalls in E. coli.
source: Evidence supporting this model has been found in the context of EF-P dependent polyproline stalls in E. coli (Hersch et al., 2014; Woolstenhulme et al., 2015), and rare-codon induced pausing in E. coli and yeast (Mitarai et al., 2008; Chu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: Evidence supporting the traffic jam model has been found in the context of rare-codon induced pausing in E. coli and yeast.
source: Evidence supporting this model has been found in the context of EF-P dependent polyproline stalls in E. coli (Hersch et al., 2014; Woolstenhulme et al., 2015), and rare-codon induced pausing in E. coli and yeast (Mitarai et al., 2008; Chu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: In the abortive termination model, ribosome stalling causes premature termination without synthesis of the full-length protein.
source: In an alternate abortive termination model, ribosome stalling causes premature termination without synthesis of the full-length protein.
evidence: This claim describes a mechanistic model that is discussed in the manuscript.

claim: The abortive termination model is thought to underlie the action of various ribosome rescue factors in E. coli and yeast.
source: This model is thought to underlie the action of various ribosome rescue factors in E. coli and yeast (Subramaniam et al., 2014; Choe et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ribosome stalling can affect protein expression indirectly by altering mRNA stability.
source: Finally, ribosome stalling can also affect protein expression indirectly by altering mRNA stability (Presnyak et al., 2015; Radhakrishnan et al., 2016), co-translational protein folding (Chaney and Clark, 2015), or stress-response signaling (Ishimura et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ribosome stalling can affect protein expression indirectly by altering co-translational protein folding.
source: Finally, ribosome stalling can also affect protein expression indirectly by altering mRNA stability (Presnyak et al., 2015; Radhakrishnan et al., 2016), co-translational protein folding (Chaney and Clark, 2015), or stress-response signaling (Ishimura et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ribosome stalling can affect protein expression indirectly by altering stress-response signaling.
source: Finally, ribosome stalling can also affect protein expression indirectly by altering mRNA stability (Presnyak et al., 2015; Radhakrishnan et al., 2016), co-translational protein folding (Chaney and Clark, 2015), or stress-response signaling (Ishimura et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Certain codons that are cognate to the limiting amino acid decrease protein expression during starvation for single amino acids in E. coli.
source: During starvation for single amino acids in E. coli, certain codons that are cognate to the limiting amino acid decrease protein expression, while the same codons have little or no effect during nutrient-rich growth (Subramaniam et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: Synonymously mutating seven CTG leucine codons in the yellow fluorescent protein gene (yfp) to CTA, CTC, or CTT reduced the synthesis rate of YFP 10–100 fold during leucine starvation.
source: For example, synonymously mutating seven CTG leucine codons in the yellow fluorescent protein gene (yfp) to CTA, CTC, or CTT reduced the synthesis rate of YFP 10–100 fold during leucine starvation (Subramaniam et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: Genome-wide ribosome profiling showed that ribosomes stall at CTA, CTC, and CTT codons during leucine starvation.
source: Genome-wide ribosome profiling showed that ribosomes stall at CTA, CTC, and CTT codons during leucine starvation, which leads to a traffic jam of trailing ribosomes and abortive termination of translation (Subramaniam et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: Ribosome stalling at CTA, CTC, and CTT codons during leucine starvation leads to a traffic jam of trailing ribosomes and abortive termination of translation.
source: Genome-wide ribosome profiling showed that ribosomes stall at CTA, CTC, and CTT codons during leucine starvation, which leads to a traffic jam of trailing ribosomes and abortive termination of translation (Subramaniam et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: A single CTA codon at two different locations reduced YFP expression during leucine starvation by 3–4 fold relative to a control yfp without CTA codons.
source: While YFP expression was similar across all yfp variants during leucine-rich growth, a single CTA codon at two different locations reduced YFP expression during leucine starvation by 3–4 fold relative to a control yfp without CTA codons (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Introducing both CTA codons reduced YFP expression by ~6 fold during leucine starvation.
source: Introducing both CTA codons reduced YFP expression by ~6 fold (Figure 1B), and a stretch of 7 CTA codons reduced YFP expression close to background level as observed in our earlier work (Subramaniam et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A stretch of 7 CTA codons reduced YFP expression close to background level during leucine starvation.
source: Introducing both CTA codons reduced YFP expression by ~6 fold (Figure 1B), and a stretch of 7 CTA codons reduced YFP expression close to background level as observed in our earlier work (Subramaniam et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and a citation to previous work.

claim: Polysome fractionation of leucine-starved E. coli did not indicate an unambiguous shift of the yfp mRNA to higher polysome fractions when two stall-inducing CTA codons were introduced 475nt from the start codon.
source: However, polysome fractionation of leucine-starved E. coli did not indicate an unambiguous shift of the yfp mRNA to higher polysome fractions when two stall-inducing CTA codons were introduced 475nt from the start codon (Figure 1C, top vs bottom panels).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Previous ribosome density measurements detected traffic jams of only 1–2 ribosomes behind stalled ribosomes.
source: This observation agrees with previous ribosome density measurements that detected traffic jams of only 1–2 ribosomes behind stalled ribosomes (Subramaniam et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: Truncated YFP fragments consistent with abortive termination at stall-inducing CTA codons were detected during leucine starvation.
source: We detected truncated YFP fragments consistent with abortive termination at stall-inducing CTA codons during leucine starvation (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D (Western blot).

claim: Previous studies suggested that abortive termination of stalled ribosomes requires cleavage of mRNA near the stall site as an obligatory step.
source: Previous studies suggested that abortive termination of stalled ribosomes requires cleavage of mRNA near the stall site as an obligatory step (Keiler, 2015; Hayes and Sauer, 2003; Ivanova et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: yfp mRNA levels, as measured by quantitative RT-PCR spanning the single CTA codons, did not decrease significantly during leucine starvation.
source: However, we found that yfp mRNA levels, as measured by quantitative RT-PCR spanning the single CTA codons, did not decrease significantly during leucine starvation (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Introducing two CTA codons resulted in <2 fold decrease in yfp mRNA levels despite ~6 fold decrease in YFP expression.
source: Similarly, introducing two CTA codons resulted in <2 fold decrease in yfp mRNA levels despite ~6 fold decrease in YFP expression (Figure 1E vs 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1E and 1B.

claim: Earlier measurements using ribosome profiling and Northern blotting did not find evidence for significant mRNA cleavage or decay upon ribosome stalling at CTA codons during leucine starvation.
source: These observations are consistent with earlier measurements using ribosome profiling and Northern blotting that did not find evidence for significant mRNA cleavage or decay upon ribosome stalling at CTA codons during leucine starvation (Subramaniam et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: In the SAT model, varying the initiation rate does not modulate the effect of the stall site on protein synthesis rate.
source: In the SAT model, varying the initiation rate does not modulate the effect of the stall site on protein synthesis rate (Figure 3A, blue squares).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In the TJ and CSAT models, the effect of the stall site on protein synthesis rate is reduced at lower initiation rates.
source: By contrast, in the TJ and CSAT models, the effect of the stall site on protein synthesis rate is reduced at lower initiation rates (Figure 3A, green circles and red diamonds).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In the traffic jam (TJ) model, additional stall sites had very little effect on protein synthesis rate.
source: In the traffic jam (TJ) model, additional stall sites had very little effect on protein synthesis rate (Figure 3B, green circles).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the simple abortive termination (SAT) model, protein synthesis rate decreased exponentially with the number of stall sites.
source: In the simple abortive termination (SAT) model, protein synthesis rate decreased exponentially with the number of stall sites (Figure 3B, blue squares).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the collision-stimulated abortive termination (CSAT) model, the effect of additional stall sites was intermediate between the TJ and SAT models.
source: In the collision-stimulated abortive termination (CSAT) model, the effect of additional stall sites was intermediate between the TJ and SAT models (Figure 3B, red diamonds).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In the SAT model, varying the distance between two stall sites does not modulate the effect of the stall sites on protein synthesis rate.
source: In the SAT model, varying the distance between two stall sites does not modulate the effect of the stall sites on protein synthesis rate (Figure 3C, blue).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 3C.

claim: In the CSAT model, when the two stall sites are separated by less than a ribosome footprint, then the frequency of collisions at the stall sites increases, thus resulting in the lower protein synthesis rate in this regime.
source: In the CSAT model, when the two stall sites are separated by less than a ribosome footprint, then the frequency of collisions at the stall sites increases, thus resulting in the lower protein synthesis rate in this regime (Figure 3C, red).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The effect of a single CTA codon on YFP synthesis rate decreased as the initiation rate of the yfp variants was reduced.
source: The effect of a single CTA codon on YFP synthesis rate decreased as the initiation rate of the yfp variants was reduced (Figure 4, black triangles).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Both the TJ and CSAT models predicted the decreasing effect of the CTA codon with lower initiation rate.
source: Both the TJ and CSAT models predicted the decreasing effect of the CTA codon with lower initiation rate (Figure 4, green circles and red diamonds).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 4.

claim: The predicted YFP synthesis rate from the SAT model was independent of initiation rate.
source: By contrast, the predicted YFP synthesis rate from the SAT model was independent of initiation rate (Figure 4, blue squares).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 4.

claim: The TJ model systematically overestimated the YFP synthesis rate for 12 of 13 multiple-CTA variants.
source: We found that the TJ model systematically overestimated the YFP synthesis rate for 12 of 13 multiple-CTA variants (Figure 5, green circles), while the SAT model systematically underestimated the YFP synthesis rate for all 13 multiple-CTA variants during leucine starvation (Figure 5, blue squares).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of simulation predictions with experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The SAT model systematically underestimated the YFP synthesis rate for all 13 multiple-CTA variants during leucine starvation.
source: We found that the TJ model systematically overestimated the YFP synthesis rate for 12 of 13 multiple-CTA variants (Figure 5, green circles), while the SAT model systematically underestimated the YFP synthesis rate for all 13 multiple-CTA variants during leucine starvation (Figure 5, blue squares).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of simulation predictions with experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The predicted YFP synthesis rates from the CSAT model were closest to the measured YFP synthesis rates with approximately half the average error of the TJ and SAT models.
source: By contrast, the predicted YFP synthesis rates from the CSAT model (Figure 5, red diamonds) were closest to the measured YFP synthesis rates with approximately half the average error of the TJ and SAT models.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of simulation predictions with experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Two CTA codons separated by less than a ribosome footprint (d < 10 codons) resulted in lower protein synthesis rate than two CTA codons separated by several ribosome footprints (d > 50 codons).
source: We found that two CTA codons separated by less than a ribosome footprint (d < 10 codons) resulted in lower protein synthesis rate than two CTA codons separated by several ribosome footprints (d > 50 codons) (Figure 6, black triangles).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The CSAT model provided a better fit than either the TJ or SAT models overall for the distance between stall sites experiment.
source: This observation was in line with the predictions from the TJ and CSAT models (Figure 3C), with the CSAT model providing a better fit than either the TJ or SAT models overall.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of simulation predictions with experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The TJ model systematically overestimates the measured YFP synthesis rate (p<10–15, one-sided Student's t-test).
source: Combining the results from all the yfp mutants (N = 94) and assuming independent and normal distribution of residual errors, we conclude that the TJ model systematically overestimates the measured YFP synthesis rate (p<10–15, one-sided Student's t-test), while the SAT model systematically underestimates the measured YFP synthesis rate (p<10–8, one-sided Student's t-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of all experimental data (N=94 mutants).

claim: The SAT model systematically underestimates the measured YFP synthesis rate (p<10–8, one-sided Student's t-test).
source: Combining the results from all the yfp mutants (N = 94) and assuming independent and normal distribution of residual errors, we conclude that the TJ model systematically overestimates the measured YFP synthesis rate (p<10–15, one-sided Student's t-test), while the SAT model systematically underestimates the measured YFP synthesis rate (p<10–8, one-sided Student's t-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of all experimental data (N=94 mutants).

claim: The CSAT model shows no systematic bias (p>0.05, two-sided Student's t-test).
source: The CSAT model shows no such bias (p>0.05, two-sided Student's t-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of all experimental data.

claim: Using the Akaike Information Criterion, there is an Akaike weight >0.999 in favor of the CSAT model over the TJ and SAT models.
source: Under the same assumption of normal distribution of residual errors and using the Akaike Information Criterion (Burnham and Anderson, 2013), we find an Akaike weight >0.999 in favor of the CSAT model over the TJ and SAT models.
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis using the Akaike Information Criterion.

claim: The CSAT model provides a better fit to the measured YFP synthesis rates from the yfp mutants than either the TJ or the SAT models when the initiation rate, the number of stall sites, and the distance between stall sites are systematically varied during starvation for single amino acids in E. coli.
source: Thus we conclude that the CSAT model provides a better fit to the measured YFP synthesis rates from the yfp mutants than either the TJ or the SAT models when the initiation rate, the number of stall sites, and the distance between stall sites are systematically varied during starvation for single amino acids in E. coli.
evidence: This claim is supported by the comprehensive statistical analysis of all experimental data.

claim: Only a small fraction of ribosomes are expected to prematurely terminate from mRNAs without stall sites.
source: First, only a small fraction of ribosomes are expected to prematurely terminate from mRNAs without stall sites (Subramaniam et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2010; Sin et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Predicted protein synthesis rates from reporters without stall sites did not decrease when the abortive termination rate was increased in the CSAT model.
source: Consistent with this expectation, predicted protein synthesis rates from reporters without stall sites did not decrease when the abortive termination rate was increased in the CSAT model (Figure 7A, top panel, red).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Protein synthesis rates from reporters without stall sites decreased with increasing abortive termination rate in a SAT model in which abortive termination was not explicitly specified to be selective for stalled ribosomes.
source: By contrast, protein synthesis rates from reporters without stall sites decreased with increasing abortive termination rate in a SAT model in which abortive termination was not explicitly specified to be selective for stalled ribosomes (Figure 7A, top panel, blue vs. pink).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The frequency of abortive termination is known to be robust to over-expression of factors that rescue stalled ribosomes.
source: Second, the frequency of abortive termination is known to be robust to over-expression of factors that rescue stalled ribosomes (Moore and Sauer, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Increasing the abortive termination rate in the CSAT model predicted only a minor effect on protein synthesis rate from an mRNA with a single stall site.
source: Consistent with this observation, we found that increasing the abortive termination rate in the CSAT model predicted only a minor effect on protein synthesis rate from an mRNA with a single stall site (Figure 7A, bottom panel, red).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In both the selective and non-selective SAT models, protein synthesis rate from an mRNA with a single stall site continuously decreased as the abortive termination rate was increased.
source: By contrast, in both the selective and non-selective SAT models, protein synthesis rate from an mRNA with a single stall site continuously decreased as the abortive termination rate was increased (Figure 7A, bottom panel, blue and pink).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Previous ribosome profiling measurements have detected a queue of only a few ribosomes at CTA codons during leucine starvation in E. coli.
source: Finally, previous ribosome profiling measurements have detected a queue of only a few ribosomes at CTA codons during leucine starvation in E. coli (Subramaniam et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: The length of ribosome queues at the stall site predicted by the CSAT model is limited to a few ribosomes even when the stall site is located ~200 codons from the start codon.
source: Consistent with this observation, the length of ribosome queues at the stall site predicted by the CSAT model is limited to a few ribosomes even when the stall site is located ~200 codons from the start codon (Figure 7B, red).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The TJ model predicts a queue of ~20 ribosomes when stall sites are located ~200 codons from the start codon.
source: By contrast, the TJ model predicts a queue of ~20 ribosomes when stall sites are located ~200 codons from the start codon (Figure 7B, green).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Ribosome profiling studies have revealed a queue of only a few ribosomes at stall sites in vivo.
source: While queues of ~7 ribosomes have been detected in vitro (Wolin and Walter, 1988), ribosome profiling studies have revealed a queue of only a few ribosomes at stall sites in vivo (Woolstenhulme et al., 2015; Subramaniam et al., 2014; Guydosh and Green, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Queues of ~7 ribosomes have been detected in vitro.
source: While queues of ~7 ribosomes have been detected in vitro (Wolin and Walter, 1988), ribosome profiling studies have revealed a queue of only a few ribosomes at stall sites in vivo (Woolstenhulme et al., 2015; Subramaniam et al., 2014; Guydosh and Green, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Recent studies on EF-P dependent pauses in bacteria and rare-codon dependent pauses in yeast suggested that the TJ model underlies the decreased protein expression when stall sites are over 100 codons away from the start codon.
source: Nevertheless, recent studies on EF-P dependent pauses in bacteria and rare-codon dependent pauses in yeast suggested that the TJ model underlies the decreased protein expression when stall sites are over 100 codons away from the start codon (Hersch et al., 2014; Chu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Collision-stimulated abortive termination is a plausible alternative mechanism to the traffic jam model proposed in previous studies.
source: Thus, collision-stimulated abortive termination is a plausible alternative mechanism to the traffic jam model proposed in previous studies (Hersch et al., 2014; Chu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the authors' modeling and experimental results.

claim: Simple kinetic partitioning between normal elongation and abortive termination has been proposed as a possible mechanism for how ribosome rescue factors might act at ribosomes that are stalled within an mRNA.
source: Simple kinetic partitioning between normal elongation and abortive termination has been proposed as a possible mechanism for how ribosome rescue factors might act at ribosomes that are stalled within an mRNA (Brandman and Hegde, 2016; Shao and Hegde, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A non-selective mechanism of abortive termination will result in decreased protein expression from mRNAs that do not have stall sites.
source: However, our modeling indicates that this non-selective mechanism of abortive termination will result in decreased protein expression from mRNAs that do not have stall sites (Figure 7A, top panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by simulation results shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Ribosome collisions during amino acid starvation could stimulate abortive termination through several mechanisms.
source: Ribosome collisions during amino acid starvation could stimulate abortive termination through several mechanisms.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about possible mechanisms.

claim: Ribosome collisions could either stimulate spontaneous drop-off of stalled ribosomes, or they could stimulate the activity of quality control pathways such as the tmRNA and the ArfA systems that rescue stalled ribosomes.
source: Specifically, ribosome collisions could either stimulate spontaneous drop-off of stalled ribosomes, or they could stimulate the activity of quality control pathways such as the tmRNA and the ArfA systems that rescue stalled ribosomes (Keiler, 2015; Shoemaker and Green, 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about possible mechanisms, with citations to relevant background literature.

claim: Ribosome collisions might allow the quality control pathway to selectively recognize ribosomes that have been stalled for an extended duration over ribosomes that are transiently stalled due to the stochasticity of normal elongation.
source: In the latter case, ribosome collisions might allow the quality control pathway to selectively recognize ribosomes that have been stalled for an extended duration over ribosomes that are transiently stalled due to the stochasticity of normal elongation (Miller and Buskirk, 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about a possible mechanism, with a citation to relevant background literature.

claim: The frequency of ribosome collisions can provide a natural timer for achieving selectivity of quality control pathways towards stalled ribosomes.
source: In this sense, the frequency of ribosome collisions can provide a natural timer for achieving selectivity of quality control pathways towards stalled ribosomes (Shao and Hegde, 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' modeling results, with a citation to relevant background literature.

claim: The robustness of the CSAT model to changes in the abortive termination rate can buffer against cell-to-cell variation in the concentration of quality control factors that mediate abortive termination.
source: Further, the robustness of the CSAT model to changes in the abortive termination rate (Figure 7A, bottom panel) can buffer against cell-to-cell variation in the concentration of quality control factors that mediate abortive termination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the simulation results shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Ribosome collisions might also have a role in stimulating the activity of eukaryotic translational quality control pathways such as No-Go mRNA decay.
source: Finally, ribosome collisions might also have a role in stimulating the activity of eukaryotic translational quality control pathways (C. Simms and H. Zaher, personal communication) such as No-Go mRNA decay (Doma and Parker, 2006), where the kinetic events leading to recognition of stalled ribosomes remain poorly defined (Shoemaker and Green, 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about possible mechanisms in eukaryotes, with citations to relevant background literature and a personal communication.

claim: This general role for ribosome collisions in translational quality control could have arisen during evolution to minimize the idling of translation-competent ribosomes on mRNAs.
source: This general role for ribosome collisions in translational quality control could have arisen during evolution to minimize the idling of translation-competent ribosomes on mRNAs.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about evolutionary implications.

claim: The measurements are quantitatively inconsistent with the traffic jam model that blocks initiation.
source: Our measurements are quantitatively inconsistent with two widely-used kinetic models for stalled ribosomes: ribosome traffic jams that block initiation, and abortive (premature) termination of stalled ribosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the comprehensive experimental and modeling analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The measurements are quantitatively inconsistent with the simple abortive termination model.
source: Our measurements are quantitatively inconsistent with two widely-used kinetic models for stalled ribosomes: ribosome traffic jams that block initiation, and abortive (premature) termination of stalled ribosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the comprehensive experimental and modeling analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: The measurements support a model in which collision with a trailing ribosome causes abortive termination of the stalled ribosome.
source: Rather, our measurements support a model in which collision with a trailing ribosome causes abortive termination of the stalled ribosome.
evidence: This claim is supported by the comprehensive experimental and modeling analysis presented in the manuscript.

claim: In the computational analysis, ribosome collisions selectively stimulate abortive termination without fine-tuning of kinetic rate parameters at ribosome stall sites.
source: In our computational analysis, ribosome collisions selectively stimulate abortive termination without fine-tuning of kinetic rate parameters at ribosome stall sites.
evidence: This claim is supported by the computational modeling results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ribosome collisions serve as a robust timer for translational quality control pathways to recognize stalled ribosomes.
source: We propose that ribosome collisions serve as a robust timer for translational quality control pathways to recognize stalled ribosomes.
evidence: This is a proposal based on the authors' modeling and experimental results.

claim: The selectivity of the CSAT model towards stalled ribosomes naturally arises from the requirement for ribosome collisions to cause abortive termination.
source: This selectivity towards stalled ribosomes naturally arises in the CSAT model from the requirement for ribosome collisions to cause abortive termination.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structure of the CSAT model.

claim: The robustness of the CSAT model to varying abortive termination rates arises because the frequency of ribosome collisions limit the actual rate of abortive termination at stall sites.
source: The robustness of the CSAT model to varying abortive termination rates arises because the frequency of ribosome collisions limit the actual rate of abortive termination at stall sites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structure of the CSAT model and simulation results.
